newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.
newsitem.headline: Singapore government securities end narrowly mixed.

text.p: Singapore government securities ended narrowly mixed in moderate trade on retail and interbank interest, dealers said on Tuesday.

"The interbank rate rose slightly today but there was little impact on the market. Treasury bill yields were narrowly mixed but bond prices were steady to slightly higher. Volume was moderate," a local dealer said.
In treasury bills, three-months closed at a yield of 1.56/1.51 percent compared with Monday's yield of 1.55/1.50 percent and one-year at a yield of 1.70/1.65 percent against 1.72/1.67 percent.
Among bonds, April 1998 was unchanged from Monday's close of S$99.53/99.58 and September 2001 unchanged at S$96.67/96.72.
June 2003 ended at S$94.68/94.73 versus Monday's close of S$94.67/94.72.
The interbank rate rose to 3-3/8 3-1/4 percent against Monday's 3-5/16 3-3/16 percent.
